title: Retroactive Invoice Adjustment Engine for Token Metering
creator: Priya Shah
description: Build a resilient service that applies retroactive adjustments (credits/debits) to customer invoices when upstream metering changes are detected. This engine must preserve an immutable primary ledger while emitting auditable adjustment records that surface in Console line-items and downstream billing exports. Work includes design for: 1) detecting candidates for retroactive adjustment (reconciliation diffs), 2) calculating pro-rated credit/debit amounts with timezone-aware windows, 3) generating idempotent adjustment records that reference original ledger entries, and 4) orchestrating safe rollout with feature flags and monitoring. Non-goals: invoice re-issuance automation and payment gateway interactions; this project will only surface adjustment line items for the finance team to act on.
acceptance_criteria: Retro adjustments are emitted as separate adjustment events linked to original invoice lines
Adjustments are idempotent and can be reprocessed without double-crediting
Console displays adjustment line items grouped by invoice with drilldown to source delta
Nightly batch reconciliation yields <= 0.05% unexplained delta against expected token consumption for active tenants
Audit trail (who/what/when) available for each adjustment and retained for 2 years
design_notes: We will not mutate the immutable token_ledger table; instead create adjustments table (adjustment_events) that references ledger_id and original_request_id
Detection pipeline: streaming diffs via Kafka topic 'metering.diff' + Flink job to aggregate per-tenant per-route deltas for 24h rolling windows
Fallback nightly reconciliation: Airflow DAG that joins raw ingestion, token_ledger snapshots, and platform routing logs to compute end-of-day corrections
Pricing model for retro credits implemented as the same unit_price snapshot used at original billing_time to avoid accounting mismatch
Edge case: model retries and streaming partial responses — adjustments include a 'confidence' score and will be batched for review if below threshold
schema_changes: create table adjustments (adjustment_id uuid, ledger_id uuid, tenant_id uuid, amount_cents bigint, reason text, created_by text, created_at timestamptz, original_event_time timestamptz, reference string)
add column invoice_visible boolean default false to adjustments
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (canary): enable streaming detection for 5 internal tenants, emit adjustments to staging only
Phase 2: enable adjustments emission to production but mark invoice_visible=false; finance runs dry-run exports for 2 billing cycles
Phase 3: turn on invoice_visible for low-risk customer cohort, monitor chargeback metrics for 3 cycles
Phase 4: full rollout and add auto-export to finance system behind entitlement flag
monitoring_and_alerting: SLO: adjustments processing latency <= 30m for high-confidence diffs
Alert: unexplained_delta_rate > 0.2% triggers P1 on-call rotation
Dashboard: 'Retroactive Adjustments' in Console -> Billing with per-tenant breakdown and top reasons
comments: 2026-02-11: Kickoff meeting — aligned on keeping primary ledger immutable. Action: Priya to draft Confluence spec (link: https://confluence.redwood.ai/billing/retro-adjustments-spec) and schedule architecture review.
2026-02-18: Architecture review — On-call raised concerns about adjustment storms; decided to implement per-tenant rate limiter and backpressure on Kafka topic 'metering.diff'
2026-02-24: Prototype Flink job submitted (PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/2018). Early tests show 80% reduction in false positives after applying time-window deduping logic.

2026-03-02: Finance dry-run schema agreed. Export format defined: CSV with columns (tenant_id, invoice_id, adjustment_id, amount_cents, reason, original_event_time, created_at). Confluence doc updated.
2026-03-06: Design review feedback from Product (Aisha): add 'confidence' and 'review_required' flags. Liam to update adjustment_events schema and migration plan.
2026-03-09: QA found race condition when same ledger entry reprocessed across two batch runs. Mitigation: use optimistic locking on ledger_id + processing token; added to PR.
2026-03-12: Security review kickoff scheduled; SRE suggested encryption-at-rest and tighter IAM on adjustment exports. Security ticket created: SEC-4392.
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: mass credits could cause surprise large negative invoices. Mitigation: default invoice_visible=false and manual finance approval before customer-facing exposure.
Risk: Duplicate adjustments due to replays. Mitigation: idempotency key = sha256(ledger_id || reconciliation_window_start) and store processed_keys table.
Risk: Performance impact on Stream processors. Mitigation: offload heavy joins to nightly batch and keep streaming detection lightweight (signal only)
Risk: Ambiguous price snapshots across historical model price changes. Mitigation: snapshot unit_price at time-of-consumption and persist in ledger row reference
qa_plan: Unit tests for idempotency and adjustment calculation logic
Integration test that replays 10k synthetic events through Kafka topic and validates no duplicate credits
End-to-end dry-run exports validated by Finance team against expected CSVs
Load test for Flink job to validate scaling to peak ingestion (5M events/min)
